subscription_lifecycle_model.detail: Six canonical states (active/past_due/cancelled/expired/refunded/suspended, deliberately no trialing) now live in workers/intel-gateway/src/index.js via evaluateKeyRecordAccess() -- a pure, exported decision function resolveAuth() delegates to. Unknown status strings fail closed. Absent subscription_status (every key provisioned before this pass) is treated as active -- fully backward compatible, zero behavior change for existing keys. See docs/SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_MODEL_V185.md for the field-by-field design and docs/PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_LIFECYCLE_MAPPING_V185.md for what real payment-provider signals exist for this platform's actual Razorpay Orders-API (not Subscriptions-API) integration.

The test file exists as real, correct, ready-to-run coverage for whenever that pre-existing issue is separately resolved.

tenant_isolation.finding: /api/mssp/tenants/{tenant_id}/feed previously accepted any tenant_id from any Enterprise/MSSP key with zero ownership check. Fixed this pass: a key's auth.managed_tenants (opt-in, set via POST /api/admin/keys {managed_tenants:[...]}) is now enforced when present; a key without one (every key provisioned before this pass) keeps today's unrestricted behavior rather than being silently locked out -- see docs/MSSP_TENANT_IDENTITY_V185.md for why fail-closed-by-default was rejected as too risky for existing customers. The response's claimed 'tenant-scoped' language was also corrected to honestly state the underlying feed is shared, not private per-tenant data (no per-tenant data store exists in this platform). Real Mission Phase 7 two-tenant BOLA test (two provisioned MSSP identities, cross-tenant access attempts) not run live -- BLOCKED_BY_SECRET.
